classification.difficultyReason: Requires an auxiliary construction and a congruence proof using equal radii and isosceles-triangle angles.

content.prompt: In this circle $\angle BAO=\angle CAO$. Prove $AB=AC$. Suggestion: Construct $BC$.

spec.description: Circle with centre O, top point A, lower circumference points B and C, chords AB and AC, and a vertical diameter through A and O. Matching angle arcs and filled dots mark the two equal angles at A. BC is absent.
spec.mathematics: A, B and C lie on the circle; O is its centre; angle BAO equals angle CAO.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible. The requested construction BC and proof radii OB and OC are not supplied.

answer.worked:
Construct $BC$ and join $OB$ and $OC$.

$OA=OB=OC$ (radii), so $\triangle OAB$ and $\triangle OAC$ are isosceles. Thus $\angle ABO=\angle BAO$ and $\angle ACO=\angle CAO$.

Since $\angle BAO=\angle CAO$ (given), $\angle ABO=\angle ACO$. Also, $OA$ is common.

Therefore, $\triangle OAB\cong\triangle OAC$ (AAS), so $AB=AC$ (corresponding sides).
